value: Elevated in HTN: Prevotella, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Fusobacterium, stearic acid

biomarker_value.notes: Specific biomarker changes documented across disease states and in FMT recipient mice.

extraction_warnings: Schema requests sample-level data with unique subject_id and sample_id, but the paper reports only aggregated cohort-level statistics (n=41 controls, n=56 pHTN, n=99 HTN from 196 participants). No per-sample rows with individual identifiers are provided in the accessible sections.
Age is reported as study-level aggregate (not reported in detail per individual); inferred Adult based on context (Kailuan Group employees, newly diagnosed hypertensive patients).
Sex distribution is noted as discrepant among groups but specific per-sample values are not reported.
Individual BMI, age, and ancestry values are not reported per sample; only group-level statistics are provided.
Antibiotics exclusion criterion (within last 8 weeks) applied to all participants; assumed 'No' for antibiotics_current_use at baseline.
The paper lacks explicit subject_id and sample_id fields. Sample stratification follows the three reported cohorts (control, pHTN, HTN) rather than individual samples.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Healthy controls', 'Pre-hypertension (pHTN)', 'Primary hypertension (HTN)', 'HTN mice (FMT recipients)', 'Control mice (FMT recipients)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.

Study involves three human FMT donors (2 HTN, 1 control) and recipient germ-free mice groups; human donor identifiers and detailed clinical characteristics are minimally provided (Additional file 11: Table S17 referenced but not fully shown in provided text).
Metagenomic and metabolomic data are reported at aggregate study/subgroup level; no individual participant-level microbiota or metabolite profiles are provided in the main text.

Multiple biomarker fields (biomarker_name, biomarker_unit, biomarker_value) are populated with summary information about bacterial taxa and metabolites identified as dysbiotic in disease, rather than per-sample measurements; granularity is subgroup_level.
Treatment field indicates participants were treatment-naive for antihypertensives but other medications (statins, aspirin, etc.) were excluded; complete medication history not fully detailed.
FMT recipient mice BP measurements (SBP, DBP, MBP, HR) obtained 10 weeks post-transplantation; only post-procedure measurements provided (no pre-transplant baseline in germ-free state).
Smoking status reflects exclusion criterion; all enrolled human participants classified as non-smokers (smoking patients excluded).

Neonatal fields (birth weight, delivery method, gestational age, preterm status, feeding) are not applicable; study enrolls adult employees (age range not explicitly provided but cohort from Kailuan Group Corporation).
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Field 'tumor_size_residual_measurement' is not applicable to this hypertension/microbiota study.
The paper describes a single prospective cohort study (Kailuan), not multiple independent studies, so 'study_name' is singular.
Host species field contains two values because the study involves both human participants (metagenomic/metabolomic analyses) and germ-free mice (transplantation experiments).

The sequencing platform for 16S rRNA analysis of recipient mice was 'Illumina HiSeq' (V4 region, 250 bp reads), matching the metagenomic platform used for human samples, though distinct from the shotgun metagenomic sequencing parameters (125 bp paired-end reads) for the primary human cohort.
